## What it is

The Audit and Accountability policy states what the organization requires for audit and accountability and who is accountable for it. It meets [AU-1](/controls/au/au-1/) through the sections every family policy shares, and adds one statement group per control. Each baseline variant includes only the controls in that baseline, taken from the NIST SP 800-53B profiles.

Adopt the ready-to-adopt edition: fill every highlighted field, delete any "Federal systems" section that does not apply, and have the accountable official approve it. The annotated edition adds guidance on why each section exists and what assessors look for.

## Decisions to make first

The policy has 44 organization-defined parameters across all variants; each appears as a highlighted field with its typical value where one is given. Settle these first:

| Decision | Controls | Typical | Who decides |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Where are audit records collected, and who operates that platform? | [AU-6(1)](/controls/au/au-6/#au-6.1), [AU-9(2)](/controls/au/au-9/#au-9.2) | A central log platform or SIEM run by the security operations team, separate from the systems it collects from. | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Which event types does every system log as a minimum? | [AU-2](/controls/au/au-2/), [AU-12](/controls/au/au-12/) | The list in the audit logging standard, reviewed annually. | Chief Information Security Officer |

Record your values in the [Audit and Accountability decision worksheet](/templates/worksheets/au/), which lists every parameter with its typical value.

## Preview (Moderate baseline, annotated)

:::note[Guidance]
The sections before and after Policy statements meet AU-1, which asks for a policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination and compliance, plus procedures, dissemination, a designated official and a review cycle. Assessors check each element, so keep every section even when it is short. Each statement cites the AU-1 item it meets. If you adopt several family policies, the same sections repeat in each; that is expected, and it lets each policy stand alone.
:::

### Purpose

This policy states what <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span> requires for Audit and Accountability, and who is accountable for meeting those requirements. (AU-1a.1(a))

### Scope

This policy applies at the <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: organization-level; mission/business process-level; system-level</span> to every system that <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span> owns or operates, or that is operated on its behalf, and to every person with access to those systems, including employees, contractors and partners. (AU-1a.1(a))

### Roles and responsibilities

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> is accountable for this policy and shall approve exceptions to it. (AU-1a.1(a))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the audit and accountability policy and procedures</span> shall manage the development, documentation and dissemination of this policy and its procedures. (AU-1b)
- Each <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall implement this policy for their system and document how in the system security plan. (AU-1a.1(a))
- Each person within scope shall follow this policy and report suspected violations to the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span>. (AU-1a.1(a))

### Management commitment

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> approves this policy and shall provide the resources needed to implement it. (AU-1a.1(a))

### Coordination

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall coordinate this policy with the legal, privacy, human resources and procurement functions, and with the owners of related policies, before each approval. (AU-1a.1(a))

### Compliance

- This policy shall be consistent with the laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards and guidelines that apply to <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span>, including <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: laws, regulations and standards that apply to the organization</span>. (AU-1a.1(b))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall review compliance with this policy through the organization's assessment and continuous monitoring activities. (AU-1a.1(a))
- An exception to this policy shall be requested in writing, approved by the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span>, time-limited and recorded with its compensating measures. (AU-1a.1(a))
- Violations of this policy shall be handled through the organization's sanctions process. (AU-1a.1(a))

### Procedures

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the audit and accountability policy and procedures</span> shall ensure that documented procedures exist to implement this policy and its associated controls. (AU-1a.2)

### Dissemination

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the audit and accountability policy and procedures</span> shall disseminate this policy to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to whom the audit and accountability policy is to be disseminated</span>. (AU-1a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the audit and accountability policy and procedures</span> shall disseminate the procedures that implement this policy to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to whom the audit and accountability procedures are to be disseminated</span>. (AU-1a)

### Policy statements

:::note[Guidance]
Each statement below comes from the clause for one control or enhancement in the chosen baseline. The reference at the end of each statement names the control item it meets.
:::

#### Event logging (AU-2)

:::note[Guidance]
AU-2 asks for two lists: every event type the system can log, and the subset you actually log, with a reason the subset is enough to investigate an incident. Keep both in the audit logging standard so every system starts from the same list. Assessors ask for the rationale (AU-2d) more often than any other item.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall identify <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the event types that the system is capable of logging in support of the audit function <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: logons and logoffs, account and privilege changes, use of privileged functions, access to security-relevant files, configuration changes, and security tool events</span></span> as the event types the system is capable of logging in support of the audit function. (AU-2a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall coordinate the event logging function with the other organizational entities that need audit-related information, to inform which events are logged. (AU-2b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall specify <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: event types (subset of the event types defined in AU-2a.) along with the frequency of (or situation requiring) logging for each identified event type <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the event types listed in the audit logging standard, each logged whenever it occurs</span></span> for logging within the system. (AU-2c)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall document why the event types selected for logging are adequate to support after-the-fact investigation of incidents. (AU-2d)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall review and update the event types selected for logging <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency of event types selected for logging are reviewed and updated <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: annually and after a significant incident or system change</span></span>. (AU-2e)

#### Content of audit records (AU-3)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure audit records establish what type of event occurred, when and where it occurred, its source, its outcome, and the identity of any individuals, subjects or objects associated with it. (AU-3)

#### Additional audit information (AU-3(1))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system generates audit records that also contain <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: additional information to be included in audit records <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: session and request identifiers, source and destination addresses, and the full command line for privileged commands</span></span>. (AU-3(1))

#### Audit log storage capacity (AU-4)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall allocate audit log storage capacity to accommodate <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: audit log retention requirements <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the retention period set under AU-11, with room for a year of growth</span></span>. (AU-4)

#### Response to audit logging process failures (AU-5)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system alerts <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles receiving audit logging process failure alerts <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the system administrators and the security operations team</span></span> within <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: time period for personnel or roles receiving audit logging process failure alerts <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: 1 hour</span></span> of an audit logging process failure. (AU-5a)
- When an audit logging process fails, the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: additional actions to be taken in the event of an audit logging process failure <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: restore logging and record the gap in the audit trail; for high-impact systems, stop processing that cannot be logged</span></span>. (AU-5b)

#### Audit record review, analysis and reporting (AU-6)

:::note[Guidance]
Most findings under AU-6 are about evidence, not effort: the review happened but left no record. Keep a dated record of each review with what was looked at, what was found and who it was reported to.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> shall review and analyze system audit records <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: frequency at which system audit records are reviewed and analyzed <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: continuously through automated alerting, with a documented manual review at least weekly</span></span> for indications of <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: inappropriate or unusual activity <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the activity listed in the log review procedure, such as repeated failed logons, privilege escalation and access outside normal patterns</span></span> and its potential impact. (AU-6a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> shall report findings to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to receive findings from reviews and analyses of system records <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the system owner and the incident response team</span></span>. (AU-6b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> shall adjust the level of audit record review, analysis and reporting when law enforcement information, intelligence information or other credible sources indicate a change in risk. (AU-6c)

#### Automated process integration (AU-6(1))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> shall integrate audit record review, analysis and reporting processes using <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: automated mechanisms used for integrating audit record review, analysis, and reporting processes <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: a security information and event management (SIEM) platform</span></span>. (AU-6(1))

#### Correlate audit record repositories (AU-6(3))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Security operations team</span> shall analyze and correlate audit records across repositories to gain organization-wide situational awareness. (AU-6(3))

#### Audit record reduction and report generation (AU-7)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall provide and implement an audit record reduction and report generation capability that supports on-demand review, analysis and reporting and after-the-fact investigation of incidents. (AU-7a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure that capability does not alter the original content or time ordering of audit records. (AU-7b)

#### Automatic processing (AU-7(1))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall provide and implement the capability to process, sort and search audit records for events of interest based on <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: fields within audit records that can be processed, sorted, or searched <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: event type, time, source and destination, user identity, outcome and system component</span></span>. (AU-7(1))

#### Time stamps (AU-8)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system uses internal system clocks to generate time stamps for audit records. (AU-8a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure audit record time stamps meet a granularity of <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: granularity of time measurement for audit record timestamps <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: one second or finer</span></span> and use Coordinated Universal Time, a fixed offset from it, or include the local offset in the time stamp. (AU-8b)

#### Protection of audit information (AU-9)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall protect audit information and audit logging tools from unauthorized access, modification and deletion. (AU-9a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to be alerted upon detection of unauthorized access, modification, or deletion of audit information <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the security operations team and the system owner</span></span> are alerted when unauthorized access, modification or deletion of audit information is detected. (AU-9b)

#### Access by subset of privileged users (AU-9(4))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall authorize access to management of audit logging functionality only for <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: a subset of privileged users or roles authorized to access management of audit logging functionality <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the security operations administrators, who do not administer the systems being audited</span></span>. (AU-9(4))

#### Audit record retention (AU-11)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall retain audit records for <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: a time period to retain audit records that is consistent with the records retention policy <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: at least one year, or longer where the records retention schedule or a law requires it</span></span> to support after-the-fact investigation of incidents and to meet regulatory and organizational retention requirements. (AU-11)

#### Audit record generation (AU-12)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: system components that provide an audit record generation capability for the events types (defined in AU-02_ODP[02]) <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: all servers, network devices, security tools, databases and applications in the system boundary</span></span> provide an audit record generation capability for the event types identified under AU-2a. (AU-12a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall allow only <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles allowed to select the event types that are to be logged by specific components of the system <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the system administrators, with the security operations team approving changes</span></span> to select the event types logged by specific components of the system. (AU-12b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system generates audit records for the event types specified under AU-2c, with the content required by AU-3. (AU-12c)

### Review and update

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the audit and accountability policy and procedures</span> shall review and update this policy <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which the current audit and accountability policy is reviewed and updated</span> and following <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: events that would require the current audit and accountability policy to be reviewed and updated</span>. (AU-1c.1)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the audit and accountability policy and procedures</span> shall review and update the procedures that implement this policy <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which the current audit and accountability procedures are reviewed and updated</span> and following <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: events that would require audit and accountability procedures to be reviewed and updated</span>. (AU-1c.2)

<div class="tpl-federal">

#### Federal systems

For federal information systems, this policy also carries out the agency's information security responsibilities under the Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 ([44 U.S.C. § 3554](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title44-section3554&num=0&edition=prelim), Federal agency responsibilities) and [OMB Circular A-130](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/legacy_drupal_files/omb/circulars/A130/a130revised.pdf), Appendix I, Responsibilities for Protecting and Managing Federal Information Resources.

- Where the agency's organization-wide policy sets a value for a parameter in this policy, each system shall use that value or a stricter one. (AU-1a.1(b))

</div>
